newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. committed to Kuwait security , says general.
newsitem.headline: U.S. committed to Kuwait security , says general.

text.p: The commander of U.S. forces in the Gulf, General Binford Peay III, told Kuwaiti leaders on Saturday that Washington was committed to the Gulf Arab state's security and stability, the Kuwaiti News Agency (KUNA) said.
Peay reviewed ties including military links in talks with Kuwait's Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah and other top official, it added.
He arrived in Kuwait from Bahrain earlier in the day as part of a regional tour.
"General Peay reaffirmed during the meeting that the American administration was keen on ensuring the stability of the Gulf," KUNA said.
Kuwait, which has a defence pact with the United States, has been home to hundreds of U.S. troops since the 1991 Gulf War.

Earlier, in the Bahraini capital, Manama, Peay told a news conference Washington would send a frigate to the Gulf region in July to help boost the U.S. Navy there, Bahrain's Gulf News Agency (GNA) said. He gave no further details.

"The United States central command forces are watching the region closely to maintain security and stability and counter all dangers and challenges that might face it in general," GNA quoted Peay as saying.
Gulf Arab states have increasingly looked to the United States for protection from potential security threats from Iran and Iraq since the Gulf War.
Half a million mostly American soldiers landed on Saudi soil to launch attacks on Iraqi troops during the Gulf War that ended Iraq's seven-month occupation of Kuwait.
The United States has close to 30,000 troops in the immediate area and more than 350 warplanes deployed either on warships or in Gulf Arab states.
Peay stressed the need for Iraq to adhere to U.N. resolutions related to the Gulf War, GNA said.
"Otherwise, sanctions will remain imposed on Iraq," he said.
